 JUDGMENT
The Petitioner filed this petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of Petitioner's case, are as under:
On 14.06.2022 at about 03.45 p.m, the Petitioner was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03/KH-1478 proceeding on Margondahalli village road, Bidarahalli hobli,
Bangalore district, when he reached near Oceanus Tranquil Apartment, at that time driver of School Bus bearing Reg No.KA-53/A- 6898 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, without giving any signal or indication came at extreme right side and dashed to the Petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result of forced 3 SCCH - 19 MVC.5032/2022 impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Jyotsana Hospital, for first aid, then he was shifted to Chaya Hospital wherein, he took treatment as inpatient and spent Rs.1,00,000/-
towards medical expenses, transportation, food, conveyance and other charges.
4. It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the School Bus bearing Reg No.KA-53/A-6898.

Hence, the Avalahalli Police registered a case against driver of said vehicle in crime No.268/2022.
5.

It is contended that, prior to the accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was a Student studying at Jyothi College and also Skating Coach by Profession and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries he is not able to do his job and hence he had lost his bright future and also lost his earning and suffering from mental shock and agony.
The Respondent No.2 is being RC owner and Respondent No.1 is being Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this petition was filed against the respondents for claiming compensation.
7. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective Counsels and filed written statement separately.

8. Brief averments of the Written statement of Respondent No.1 are as under:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy Vijay.M vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81162639/
2 in respect of School Bus bearing Reg No.KA-53/A- 6898, this Respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.

While admitting ownership of School Bus bearing Reg No.KA-53/A-6898, this Respondent contended that, the driver of said vehicle got valid D.L. and insurance was in force as on the date of the accident.
It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the Petitioner.

Further both Respondents denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner,
medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

Bangalore district, at that time driver of one School Bus bearing Reg No. KA-53/A-6898 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, came at a high speed without giving any signal or indication came at extreme right side and dashed to the Petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.
Whether order or award?

As per the Petitioner, this accident occurred on 14-06-2022 while the Petitioner was riding his motor cycle proceeding on Margondahalli village road, Bidarahalli hobli, Bangalore district, near Oceanus Tranquil Apartment, driver of School Bus bearing Reg No.KA-53/A-6898 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.

But,
on perusal of Ex.P7 wound certificate it discloses that, "the H/o RTA is Two wheeler he was traveling was hit by a speeding four Wheeler (Car)".

23. The Learned Counsel for the Respondent submitted written arguments and contended that, as per the MLC extract dated 14-6-2022 isued by Jyotsna hospital, Bangalore the history noted as "alleged history of RTA hit by bike (Unknown person) and fell on road."

As per wound certificate dated 13-8-2022 issued by above said hospital the history noted as "alleged history of RTA on 14-6-2022 at around 4-00 p.m. near Margondanahalli Main road, when the two wheeler he was traveling was hit by a speeding four wheeler (Car).
But in the 13 SCCH - 19 MVC.5032/2022 complaint, which was lodged after 25 days of the alleged accident,the Petitioner claimed that while he was riding the motor cycle hit by a school bus.
The above said hospital had issued intimation tot he police on 8-7-2022 i.e., after 24 days of the alleged accident with different version about history of injuries.
There are glaring discrepancies in the manner of accident in different documents on different occasions.
The complaint was lodged after 25 days of the alleged accident and there was no proper explanation for the delay.

Since the vehicle, which actually caused the accident, was not traced and a false complaint was lodged against the insured vehicle after thought by twisting the facts by colluding all concerned persons in order to get compensation from the insurance company,
which is dealing with public funds.

The Petitioner had not produced separate receipts for payment of IP Bill, there is no corresponding prescriptions to the pharmacy bills and some bills do not have seal and signature of the issuing authority and author of the said documents not examined.
14 SCCH - 19 MVC.5032/2022 Hence prays to dismiss the petition with exemplary costs.

29. On perusal of all the three documents of Hospital which disclose the different history of accident i.e., one is fell from bike, 2 nd one is hit by bike, unknown person, and 3 rd one is two wheeler V/s 4 wheeler.

Further the complaint is lodged after 25 days from the date of accident, the reason for delay is that, he was unconscious and taking treatment, but as per the medical records Petitioner had sustained leg injury and no head injury, so the chance of getting unconscious is very less.
The reasons assigned for delay cannot be accepted and is not justifiable in view of three different versions regarding history of accident.

Therefore, by considering the all above said documents and 17 SCCH - 19 MVC.5032/2022 records available on record and also evidence of the witnesses it is evident that the offending vehicle School bus was not involved in the alleged accidentm and the Petitioner failed to prove his case.
